children.value: The determinant of a 2x2 matrix is:
\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix} = a d - bc
children.html: ∣abcd∣=ad−bc\begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix} = a d - bc∣∣​ac​bd​∣∣​=ad−bc

children.value:
We will use the definition of the determinant to show this must be the case!
Let’s use the first definition and pick the first row

children.html: i=1i=1i=1

∣abcd∣=(−1)1+1⋅A11M11+(−1)1+2A12M12=a∣abcd∣−b∣abcd∣=ad−bc\begin{align} \begin{vmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{vmatrix} &= (-1)^{1+1} \cdot A_{11} M_{11} + (-1)^{1+2} A_{12} M_{12} \\ &= a \begin{vmatrix} \phantom{a} & \phantom{b} \\ \phantom{c} & d \end{vmatrix} - b \begin{vmatrix} \phantom{a} & \phantom{b} \\ c & \phantom{d} \end{vmatrix} \\ &= a d - b c \end{align}∣∣​ac​bd​∣∣​​=(−1)1+1⋅A11​M11​+(−1)1+2A12​M12​=a∣∣​ac​bd​∣∣​−b∣∣​ac​bd​∣∣​=ad−bc​​

children.value:
The determinants of larger matrices can be computed by reducing them to sums
of 2x2 determinants. To do this quickly, it can be helpful to envision

children.value:
Even faster, start from the plus sign in the upper left corner, then alternate
until you get to your chosen row or column! Let’s use row 3:

children.html: ∣A∣=+(−1)⋅∣3064∣−0⋅∣1024∣+2⋅∣1326∣=−(3⋅4−0⋅6)+2(1⋅6−2⋅3)=−12\begin{align} |\vv{A}| &= + (-1) \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 6 & 4 \end{vmatrix} - 0 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 \end{vmatrix} + 2 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= -(3 \cdot 4 - 0 \cdot 6) + 2(1 \cdot 6 - 2 \cdot 3) \\ &= -12 \end{align}∣A∣​=+(−1)⋅∣∣​36​04​∣∣​−0⋅∣∣​12​04​∣∣​+2⋅∣∣​12​36​∣∣​=−(3⋅4−0⋅6)+2(1⋅6−2⋅3)=−12​​

children.value:
Note that the same result could be achieved using any row or column. For
example, column 3 gives:

children.html: ∣A∣=+(0)⋅∣26−10∣−4⋅∣13−10∣+2⋅∣1326∣=−4⋅(0+3)+2⋅(6−6)=−12\begin{align} |\vv{A}|&= +(0) \cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 6 \\ -1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} - 4 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ -1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} + 2 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= -4 \cdot (0+3) + 2 \cdot (6-6)\\ &= -12 \end{align}∣A∣​=+(0)⋅∣∣​2−1​60​∣∣​−4⋅∣∣​1−1​30​∣∣​+2⋅∣∣​12​36​∣∣​=−4⋅(0+3)+2⋅(6−6)=−12​​

children.value:
It’s usually a good idea to expand along the row or column with the most zeros!
For example, let’s evaluate

children.html: ∣1−200435002750020∣=−2⋅∣1−20430025∣=−2⋅5⋅∣1−243∣=−10⋅(3+8)=−110\begin{align} \begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 &2 & 7 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \end{vmatrix} &= -2 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 &2 & 5 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= -2 \cdot 5 \cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 \\ 4 & 3 \end{vmatrix} \\ &= -10 \cdot (3+8) \\ &= -110 \end{align}∣∣​1400​−2320​0572​0050​∣∣​​=−2⋅∣∣​140​−232​005​∣∣​=−2⋅5⋅∣∣​14​−23​∣∣​=−10⋅(3+8)=−110​​
